To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Chinese international students' acculturations to the U.S culture and attachment styles were related to their sociocultural adjustment.

Chinese international students with a high level of attachment anxiety and a high level of avoidance of attachment were more likely to be less acculturated to U.S. society and to have greater psychosocial adjustment difficulties than students with low levels of attachment anxiety and avoidance of attachment.
Chinese international students who are more attached to their parents and who are more acculturated to U.S. norms and values are less anxious, less avoidant, and more adjusted to U.S. society.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between attachment, acculturation, and psychosociocultural adjustment of international students.
the relationship between acculturation and attachment, and their impact on international students' adjustment.
the relationship between acculturation and psychological distress of international students.
